key_findings.1953_G_FAIL_root_cause: BOTH code and infra/VPS. CODE defects: (A) backfill column name mismatch blocks queue seeding; (B) OCR cache race across 4 independent callers with no retry. INFRA: VPS pipeline being down cannot be fixed by code. Consolidation eliminates code defects; residual staleness after fix is purely VPS/infra-owned (vpsProxyWatchdogJob escalation path).
key_findings.is_same_refactor: YES — 1954c (4 paths → 1 owner) and G5b (service as extraction owner) are structurally identical. One atomic commit set satisfies both.
key_findings.service_ownership: pdf-extractor service (port 5001) becomes PRIMARY extraction owner. In-process pdf-parse + Tesseract OCR (pdfOcrWorker.ts, pdf.ts:ocrPdfBuffer) demoted to fallback-on-service-unavailable, then deprecated.
key_findings.callers_remain_4: 4 callers (bctcPdfPullJob, pushBctcExtraction, bctcReparseJob, checkSscReports) keep independent triggers. They all route extraction through ONE service HTTP client (pdfExtractorClient.extractViaMicroservice). fetchParseAndStoreBctc (parse+store) is unchanged.

risk_flags: R-1: Service unavailable fallback must be explicit (null return → pdf-parse fallback). Mitigated by existing pdfExtractorClient null-return pattern.
R-2: 2-min service timeout already configured. No worse than existing 31-min local OCR for large scanned PDFs.
R-3: Tests injecting OCR deps must update to inject extractViaService mock. All 4 callers use injectable deps pattern — no test structural changes needed, only dep interface update.

EIB/DHG under-extraction due to scanned PDF quality (C-1: PDF structure). Service may improve this with pdfplumber+pytesseract vs local OCR.
Container OOM kill (C-2: resource pressure). Infrastructure concern, not code.
